lines.para: Between 1881 and 1885, some 15,000 Chinese workers lay the tracks of the Canadian Pacific across the Rockies. They are given the tunnels, the dynamite, the cliffs. Hundreds die there.

Once the line is finished, Ottawa no longer wants them. From 1885, every Chinese immigrant must pay a head tax: 50 dollars, then 100 in 1900, 500 in 1903, about two years’ wages. No other nationality has to pay it.
The men live alone, without wives or children. They open laundries and restaurants and band together in mutual-aid societies. Some are secret societies, born in China to overthrow the Manchu dynasty.
Sun Yat-sen tours North America several times to raise funds. In 1911, in Canada, Chinese communities mortgage their own buildings to finance the revolution.
These Chinese needed friends. They did not forget the ones they had.
